_doc: Canonical trade identity, availability and training time. training_years is the years of apprenticeship or schooling before a person is productive in the trade (an estimate of the skill, not a wage); a trade that states none takes its family's median. Wages are not stored here: sim/labour/wages.py derives them. fatality_risk_per_year is the yearly chance a worker of the trade dies at work, with fatality_source and fatality_confidence; the economy raises the wage asked for a trade by it. literate marks a trade whose practice is reading and writing, so literacy caps how many there are; taught_from is the trade a new one is taught from by default; tool_basket lists the materials a self-equipped worker replaces to stay in the trade; staff_resource names the generic staffing resource a trade fills. These four are labelled heuristics (confidence D) of the engine's labour model, moved here from code.

artisan.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

knapper.note: Strikes blades, scrapers and axes from obsidian and flint by pressure or percussion flaking (Complaint 618).
knapper.training_source: LABELLED HEURISTIC, conf D, no source found for the years it takes to learn pressure blade making. Retire: Complaint 650.
knapper.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

baker.note: Mixes, shapes and bakes bread in a masonry oven and keeps the fire. Cooks and tavern keepers are a separate owner decision (Complaint 530).
baker.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: bakers were bound as apprentices for several years in medieval guild practice (recalled, not opened); three years is a guess set beside the miller.
baker.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

carter.note: Drives a cart or leads a pack train: carter, teamster, muleteer, drover. Land carriage by animal is this trade's work; porters on foot are the porter trade.
carter.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

dockworker.note: Loads and unloads cargo at a port: stevedore, longshoreman, quay porter. Port handling hours of a sea leg are this trade's work (the sailing mode names it as its handling_trade).
dockworker.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

engineer.note: Does not exist as a paid civilian profession. A developed state may keep military and hydraulic engineers under its own employ; a private one is your invention.
engineer.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

engraver.note: Die and seal cutter. Skilled ones already exist wherever there is a minting or sealing tradition; they become your punchcutters.
engraver.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

fisher.note: Takes fish and shellfish from the sea, lakes and rivers with boat, net, line and weir. The food a society takes from the water is bounded by the hours its fishers work (sim/labour/food_gathering.py).
fisher.food_kcal_per_hour_source: Kelly 2013, The Lifeways of Hunter-Gatherers, Table 3-4: forager return rates for fish and shellfish run from a few hundred to over ten thousand kcal per hour; the low end is taken for shore and day-boat work. No source for per-boat catch was found.
fisher.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

fuller.note: Finishes cloth: scours, fulls, felts, washes, stretches and presses it. Dyeing is done by the same finishing trade but has no recipe of its own yet.
fuller.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: fulling was heavy trampling and washing in a fullonica worked largely by slaves and apprentices (recalled from Pliny, Natural History 35.57, and Roman fullonica studies, not opened), so a few years is a guess.
fuller.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

furnaceman.fatality_source: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: burns and furnace accidents; no sourced pre-industrial rate found, set an order of magnitude under mining.

glassblower.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

herder.note: Tends flocks and herds on pasture: shepherd, goatherd, cowherd, with the milking, shearing, calving and dairy work of the same household.
herder.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: herding was learned from boyhood beside a herder (recalled from pastoral ethnography, not opened); two years is a guess set beside the fisher and hunter.
herder.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

hunter.note: Hunts game with bow, spear, snare and dogs. The food a society takes from wild animals is bounded by the hours its hunters work (sim/labour/food_gathering.py).
hunter.food_kcal_per_hour_source: Kelly 2013, The Lifeways of Hunter-Gatherers, ch. 3: the Ache average from hunting alone is 1,115 kcal per hour including search time.
hunter.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

farmer.note: Grows crops and tends plantation stock on the household's own or hired land: the work the farm-labour logic sizes. Hands move between it and the unskilled labourer within a season or two, so it sits in the labourer's family; it needs no training time of its own (the labourer carries the fallback flag, so the two do not tie for fewest years).
farmer.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

labourer.note: The unskilled fallback: hauling, digging, quarrying and every task that asks no craft. Crop work is the farmer's.
labourer.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

machinist.note: Does not exist yet; you must create this trade.
machinist.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

mason.note: Abundant and good wherever there is a serious stone-building tradition; scarcer and dearer where building is mostly wood.
mason.fatality_source: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: falls from scaffolding and walls in stone building work; no sourced pre-industrial rate found, set an order of magnitude under mining.

merchant.note: Agent and factor, paid on commission in practice.
merchant.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

miller.note: Grinds and sifts grain to flour between stones, by quern, animal mill or water mill. Baking is a separate trade (Complaint 614).
miller.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: dressing the stones and setting the grind took a few years beside a miller (recalled from milling handbooks, not opened).
miller.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

millwright.note: Water-mill builder. Scarce wherever milling by water is already established; the scarcest useful trade you can hire.
millwright.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

miner.fatality_source: British Mines Inspectorate returns for coal mining, 1850s: about five fatal accidents per thousand a year, explosions alone about one per thousand (J. E. Williams/Inspectorate series as summarised in P. E. H. Hair, 'Mortality from Violence in British Coal-Mines, 1800-50', Economic History Review 21 (1968)); late-nineteenth-century metal mines ran one to two per thousand. Victorian deep coal is a high bound for earlier mining; no pre-industrial rate found.

optician.note: Does not exist yet. You must create this trade from glassworkers.
optician.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

plumber.note: Lead worker. Skilled and numerous wherever lead pipe-making is already an established trade (Roman plumbarii are the best-attested case); scarce or nonexistent elsewhere.
plumber.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

porter.note: Carries loads on the back or a tumpline over land: the Mexica tlameme, the Andean and African bearer, the hill porter. Carriage on foot is this trade's work. Trained from childhood in the carrying but asks no craft, so anyone can take it up at once.
porter.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

potter.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

sailor.fatality_source: British merchant service deaths about one in forty-eight a year in 1885 (contemporary Board of Trade return as reported in the press; primary table not checked); infectious disease at sea from M. Roberts and T. Carter, Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease (2016). Davis (1962) and Rediker (1987) give context, not the rate.

shipwright.training_source: Worshipful Company of Shipwrights, Apprenticeship Scheme leaflet, pp. 1-2 (https://www.shipwrights.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/SAScheme-2.pdf), opened: a three to four year course; four is used as a modern craft-training proxy, not an attested ancient apprenticeship length.
shipwright.note: Builds and repairs wooden hulls, including shell-first mortise-and-tenon construction.
shipwright.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

smith.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

spinner.note: Cards and spins fibre into thread or twine on a spindle or wheel, and twists strands into cordage. The slowest step of hand textile work, done by household and hired hands alike.
spinner.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: spindle spinning was learned in childhood alongside household work (recalled from the textile-history literature, e.g. Barber, Women's Work, 1994, not opened); a year to useful speed is a guess.
spinner.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

weaver.note: Warps and weaves thread into cloth on a loom (horizontal, warp-weighted, vertical or backstrap), plain or fine, silk included.
weaver.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D, set at the generic craftsman's four years it replaces for cloth: recalled guild terms for weaving ran longer (seven years under England's Statute of Artificers of 1563, not opened), which is a ceiling, not a Roman or Mexica figure.
weaver.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

charcoal_burner.note: Stacks and covers a clamp of billets, burns it slowly with little air and tends it for days, then rakes and sacks the charcoal. Fuel for smelting and smithing.
charcoal_burner.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: managing the burn of a clamp was learned over seasons beside a collier (recalled from woodland-craft accounts, not opened); two years is a guess set beside the furnaceman.
charcoal_burner.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

leatherworker.note: Cuts and stitches finished leather into shoes, harness and scabbards.
leatherworker.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: shoemakers and saddlers were bound as apprentices for several years in medieval guild practice (recalled, not opened); four years is a guess.
leatherworker.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

lime_burner.note: Builds and fires a kiln of limestone with wood or coal until it is quicklime, then draws and slakes it.
lime_burner.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: judging the burn and drawing the kiln was learned beside a lime burner (recalled from Vitruvius, De architectura II.5, and later building handbooks, not opened); two years is a guess set beside the furnaceman.
lime_burner.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

salt_worker.note: Works salt from sea and brine: fills and rakes solar pans, boils brine in lead or iron pans, and digs and breaks rock salt out of the bed.
salt_worker.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: the work is mostly hours of raking and carrying and was learned in a season (recalled, not opened).
salt_worker.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

tanner.note: Soaks, limes, scrapes and tans hides into leather in pits of bark liquor, and dresses skins into parchment and vellum.
tanner.training_source: Author's estimate, conf D: tanning was a guild trade learned over several years beside a master because pit timing decides the leather (recalled from medieval guild accounts, not opened).
tanner.fatality_source: Zero: no sourced rate for this trade was found, so it carries no danger pay. A statement of absence of data, not of safety.

soldier.note: A man under arms, drawn from the working age; the state's army is booked in this trade. Basic training is months, not years (Vegetius, De re militari 1.13 gives four months).
soldier.fatality_source: Peacetime service mortality, mostly disease: about two-fifths of Roman legionaries died during a twenty-five-year term (W. Scheidel, Measuring Sex, Age and Death in the Roman Empire, JRA Suppl. 21 (1996), ch. 3, via secondary quotation). Battle deaths are not a yearly constant and belong to the conflict mechanics.
